about: A `global` flag is recognized by the command that declares it and by everything beneath it, so it may appear before or after any subcommand word.

vectors.doc: A global flag declared at the root works before the subcommand.
The same flag works after the subcommand.
A global flag that takes a value binds it the same way at any depth.
Inheritance is not limited to one level.
`global` propagates downward only. A flag declared global on a subcommand is not accepted before that subcommand is reached.

reference.diverges: usage-lib agrees the flag is not visible here, but reports `unexpected_arg` for the same fall-through reason.

vectors.doc: A subcommand may declare its own flag with the same name as an inherited global; below that point the subcommand's flag is the one that binds. mise does this deliberately, redeclaring several root globals on `run` with different shorts.
